A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same FG-BMK study. Their main text, tables, figures, and complete appendices support comparison, including matching results moved between sections. Internal reporting discrepancies do not prevent identifying the substantive changes.

before.justification: v1 reports original recognition, retrieval, attribute-recognition, fine-tuning, alignment, and perturbation experiments in Section 4 and Appendices C–D.

after.justification: v3 retains original empirical evaluations and adds newer-model results, prompt-sensitivity experiments, and downstream alignment comparisons, including Tables 7, 8, and 15.

M1.justification: The two evaluation paradigms and granularity-matched LLaVA alignment procedure are retained. v3 Appendix D.2 explicitly evaluates variants already compared in v1 Table 4. Its suggestion of patch- or region-level contrastive objectives does not constitute an implemented method component.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same twelve source datasets listed in Table 6, the CIFAR-100 robustness comparison, and the same recognition, retrieval, attribute, hierarchy, and knowledge-bias tasks. Added model evaluations, prompt variants, and downstream alignment comparisons reuse this coverage. Revised sample totals do not establish added or removed domains.

E2.justification: v3 adds actual evaluations of InternVL3, Qwen2.5-VL, GPT-4o, and Gemini-2.0-flash. Within knowledge-bias comparisons, v1's LLaVA/Flowers102, InternVL/Stanford Dogs, and BLIP2/Aircraft experiments are replaced by GPT-4o/Flowers102, Gemini/Stanford Dogs, and Qwen2.5-VL/Aircraft experiments. The machine-oriented comparator set and specialized models in Table 3 remain unchanged.

E3.justification: Reported benchmark size changes from 3.49 million questions and 3.32 million images to 1.01 million and 0.28 million, without explaining whether this reflects resampling or revised accounting. Figure 1 and Appendix A.1 recast knowledge-bias pairing as one positive and one randomly selected negative per image. v3 also introduces a ten-template prompt experiment and downstream testing of alignment variants.

E4.justification: New Tables 7–8 test sensitivity to linguistic template diversity. Appendix D.2 and Table 15 newly examine whether the existing alignment intervention improves downstream short-answer recognition, beyond linear feature classification. Knowledge-bias analyses also replace three older fine-tuning comparisons with two closed-model bias profiles and a Qwen2.5-VL fine-tuning comparison.

E5.justification: The Friedman/Nemenyi comparisons and critical-distance plots in Figures 6–7 are retained. Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, or comparable uncertainty estimates for the experimental scores. Original-versus-extended prompt results are sensitivity comparisons, not new uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: v3 adds substantial hierarchy, attribute, knowledge-bias, and prompt-sensitivity results, and revises Figure 3's LLaVA bias curves. Table 15 adds retrained-LLaVA short-answer accuracies of 86.32% on CUB and 87.58% on Stanford Dogs, alongside retained vanilla scores of 85.60% and 86.49%; these are new variant comparisons. Tables 3–5 and the relocated older attribute and hierarchy results retain their values.

T1.justification: Neither version presents formal theorems, proofs, or substantive mathematical derivations. The evaluation concepts and standard accuracy and retrieval metrics remain unchanged; added explanations and suggested contrastive objectives introduce no formal theoretical development.

C1.justification: The abstract and introduction revise the claimed benchmark size from 3.49 million questions/3.32 million images to 1.01 million/0.28 million, and the evaluated model count from eight to twelve. The benchmark's two-perspective contribution and five headline findings remain substantively unchanged.

C2.justification: v3 adds interpretations connecting alignment-feature discriminability to downstream answers and discussing how hierarchical attention ideas could inform LVLMs. Appendix D.1 newly acknowledges residual granularity mismatch in the constructed alignment data. Conversely, v1's explicit limitations concerning medical and remote-sensing coverage are removed. The central explanations concerning training paradigms, knowledge bias, and perturbation vulnerability remain.

D1.justification: v3 newly specifies zero decoding temperature for open models, default temperatures for closed APIs, and equal image and question counts per category for balanced fine-tuning. It adds configurations for newer models and explicitly states that data splits and evaluation scripts are released, extending v1's code-release statement. These disclosures do not establish changes to previously unspecified settings.

R1.justification: References and discussion expand to include Qwen2.5-VL, InternVL3, Gemini, CAPability, and several recognition papers; FiVA and the image-to-LiDAR contrastive-distillation citation are removed. The claimed gap relative to existing fine-grained benchmarks remains unchanged. Citation-format and bibliographic updates do not constitute additional positioning changes.

P1.justification: There are targeted rewrites in related work and experimental discussion, updated author information, new ethics and reproducibility statements, and an LLM-usage appendix. The limitations paragraph is removed and some appendix cross-references are repaired. Most introductory, methodological, and concluding prose and the main section sequence are retained.

P2.justification: Figure 11 expands from three to seven panels, incorporating the relocated original Figure 2; knowledge-bias displays are replaced and split across Figures 12–13. New prompt, attribute, and downstream-alignment tables substantially expand the displays, while the original LLaVA attribute table moves to Appendix C. Model tables are restructured and the document adopts conference formatting. Most machine-oriented plots are retained.

improvement.justification: v3 strengthens the evidence through newer open and closed models, prompt-sensitivity checks, and a downstream test connecting alignment quality to recognition performance. Added decoding and balancing details improve transparency. These gains are tempered by unexplained benchmark-total revisions and unreconciled InternVL3 scores: Section 4.2 reports 90.75% genus multiple-choice accuracy, while Table 8 lists 88.13% for original prompts. The net improvement is useful but limited.
